key_insight: D^3-Subsidy is an online, sequential subsidy policy that simultaneously achieves fast responsiveness to stochastic demand/supply shocks, enforces strict per-driver subsidy-rate caps, and runs with low latency at marketplace scale—leading to measurable gains in completed rides and GMV.
problem_solved: How to optimally allocate driver-side subsidies in a large-scale ride-hailing platform under three production constraints: (i) rapid adaptation to stochastic shocks, (ii) strict subsidy-rate caps per driver, and (iii) low-latency decision making suitable for real-time operation.
method: Cast subsidy allocation as an online sequential decision problem that optimizes short-term KPIs (Rides, GMV) under stochastic demand/supply and per-driver cap constraints.

Design D^3-Subsidy to decompose decisions into fast per-event updates plus periodic global reconciliation, leveraging lightweight approximations/streaming updates to guarantee low latency and enforce caps.
Derive performance guarantees and validate the approach on large-scale ride-hailing traces and production-style experiments showing improved KPIs and scalable operation.
impact: Provides practitioners with a practical blueprint to run real-time, safe incentive policies that boost utilization and revenue while meeting regulatory/budget constraints. The approach generalizes to other two-sided marketplaces and large-scale online resource allocation problems.
visual_elements: System flow diagram: incoming requests → D^3 decision module (fast update + reconciliation) → driver incentives, annotated with latency/throughput numbers.
Before/after time-series chart showing Rides and GMV with baseline vs. D^3-Subsidy during demand shocks.
Constraint schematic: Venn or icon-based panel illustrating the three production constraints (responsiveness, subsidy caps, low latency).
Geospatial heatmap showing subsidy distribution vs. driver supply and realized ride completions.
paper_title: D$^3$-Subsidy: Online and Sequential Driver Subsidy Decision-Making for Large-Scale Ride-Hailing Market
paper_authors: Taijie Chen, Rui Su, Siyuan Feng, Laoming Zhang, Hongyang Zhang
